chapter: Kansas City bands and the Blue Devils
title: Where the names Blue Devils, Clouds of Joy and Black Aces came from
summary: They speculate on the name Blue Devils (Ellison's range-war story, blues as depression) and Durham's view that names identified black bands.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Do you know why they called it the Blue Devils?
I never did know why, no.

Because there was an article recently in the paper called Grackel where Ralph Ellison, the writer, said that in the old days, during -- when they had range wars, the people used to go and cut the barbed wire fences were called Blue Devils. I wonder if you ever heard that?
I heard that, but I didn't know the band was connected with that.
Well, it just makes you wonder whether that's where Walter Page got his title from.
I believe they named these bands, like, the Clouds of Joy, and the Blue Devils, Gene Coin's Black Aces -- I believe they were referring to color complexion.
Yeah. Because, Blue Devils, you know --
They always wanted to let you know they was a black band.
Yeah.
They always named it something that --
The Clouds of Joy --

Dark Clouds of Joy. I don't know if that name was tied with it or not. See, the clouds are dark, clouds are joy, clouds are joy. Back in those days, clouds generally come -- they dark when it's going to rain and they never think about clouds.
Yeah.
But I think it was related to identifying themselves as a black band.
Well, yeah, I would imagine --
And I thought that's what the Aces were, the Black Aces, meaning the -- you know, the ace was the top card and that guy's an ace. I think that's what they referred to.
Yeah.
Ace was supposed to be the greatest thing that was, the top card.

Well, the only thing is, you know, Blue Devils is -- when you talk of having the blues, years -- I mean, way back, 300 or 400 years ago, they used to say that a person, if he felt sick or down or depressed, they've got a case of the blue devils.
I believe part of that was --
That could mean -- I mean, some of those old things --
They did go by those terms.
Yeah, I mean, there's a lot of hangovers from much further back in the past than we sometimes are aware of, you know.
Yeah.
